1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""check_boundary.py — the ONLY script in laf-adaptation/ (ADR-006: this is a
3	validation tool, NOT a runtime). It enforces the boundary contract between the
4	ADOPTED upstream CWS subset and LAF's NATIVE / BUILD-NEW additions.
5	
6	It never transforms the framework — it only reads files, computes sha256 hashes,
7	and compares (boundary-contract.md §3, lines 18-19). The one transformation it
8	*models* (never writes) is the deterministic prefix rewrite
9	    "creative-writing-skills:" -> "laf-adaptation:"
10	
11	Modes (boundary-contract.md §3.1):
12	    check_boundary.py                       # verify (default); exit 1 on any violation
13	    check_boundary.py --init --upstream DIR # first vendor: compute hashes, write manifest rows
14	    check_boundary.py --report              # human-readable provenance summary; always exit 0
15	
16	Path rooting: all relative paths resolve against REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
17	(the laf-adaptation/ dir), so `glob("agents/*.md")` is correct no matter the caller's cwd —
18	the task invokes this from the repo root as `uv run python laf-adaptation/scripts/check_boundary.py`
19	(boundary-contract.md §3.2 uses relative globs; this rooting makes them unambiguous).
20	
21	Pure standard library only (no third-party deps — ADR-006 forbids a runtime).
22	"""
23	
24	import argparse
25	import hashlib
26	import subprocess
27	import sys
28	from pathlib import Path
29	
30	# --- Path rooting (Step 2.2 cwd-rooting contract) -------------------------------
31	REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]          # the laf-adaptation/ dir
32	VENDOR_MD = REPO / "VENDOR.md"
33	
34	# --- The deterministic prefix rewrite -------------------------------------------
35	PREFIX_FROM = "creative-writing-skills:"
36	PREFIX_TO = "laf-adaptation:"
37	
38	# --- Provenance of LAF-authored (non-upstream) files ----------------------------
39	# Adopted files are auto-detected by presence in the upstream checkout. The files
40	# below do NOT exist upstream; this closed set (DESIGN reconciled counts,
41	# constraint #8) lets --init label NATIVE vs BUILD-NEW deterministically. An
42	# existing manifest row's class is ALWAYS preserved over this map (manifest is the
43	# source of truth); the map only classifies newly-discovered non-upstream files.
44	NATIVE_AGENTS = {"analyst.md", "safety-verifier.md"}
45	BUILD_NEW_AGENTS = {"chronicler.md", "tier-coordinator.md"}
46	NATIVE_SKILLS = {"adaptation-tiers", "adaptation-rules", "source-fidelity"}
47	BUILD_NEW_SKILLS = {"adaptation-safety"}
48	
49	QUARTET = ["critic", "editor", "reader-sim", "continuity-checker"]
50	NO_HASH = "—"  # em dash marks a non-hash-pinned (NATIVE/BUILD-NEW) row
51	
52	# Manifest row classes (CH-6): a parser-validated closed set.
53	CLASSES = {"ADOPTED-CLEAN", "ADOPTED-PATCHED", "NATIVE", "BUILD-NEW"}
54	
55	
56	class ManifestError(ValueError):
57	    """Raised when a manifest row is malformed, unsafe, or self-inconsistent.
58	
59	    The parser collects these into the errors list (verify/do_init treat them as
60	    boundary-contract FAIL; --report prints them as warnings but still exits 0)."""
61	
62	
63	# --- Low-level helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
64	def sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
65	    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
66	
67	
68	def sha256_text(text: str) -> str:
69	    return sha256_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
70	
71	
72	def read_bytes(p: Path) -> bytes:
73	    return p.read_bytes()
74	
75	
76	def read_text(p: Path) -> str:
77	    return p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
78

80	def prefix_rewrite(text: str) -> str:
81	    """The one permitted vendor-time transform, recomputed (never trusted from a
82	    stored diff): replace every literal 'creative-writing-skills:' with
83	    'laf-adaptation:'."""
84	    return text.replace(PREFIX_FROM, PREFIX_TO)
85	
86	
87	def prefix_unrewrite(text: str) -> str:
88	    """Inverse of prefix_rewrite: 'laf-adaptation:' -> 'creative-writing-skills:'.
89	
90	    Used by verify-mode Rule A′ (CH-1) to re-derive the RAW upstream blob from an
91	    already-prefix-rewritten on-disk adopted body, so its hash can be compared
92	    against the pinned (PR-rewrite-resistant) `upstream_sha256`. The on-disk file
93	    IS the prefix-rewritten upstream (disk == prefix_rewrite(raw_upstream)), so
94	    prefix_unrewrite(disk) == raw_upstream for ADOPTED-CLEAN rows. For files
95	    containing no prefix literal this is a no-op (disk == raw)."""
96	    return text.replace(PREFIX_TO, PREFIX_FROM)

99	def split_frontmatter(text: str):
100	    """Return (frontmatter_lines, body_text). Frontmatter is between the first two
101	    '---' delimiter lines; body is everything after the second '---'
102	    (boundary-contract.md §3.3)."""
103	    lines = text.splitlines()
104	    if not lines or lines[0].strip() != "---":
105	        return [], text
106	    for i in range(1, len(lines)):
107	        if lines[i].strip() == "---":
108	            fm = lines[1:i]
109	            body = "\n".join(lines[i + 1:])
110	            return fm, body
111	    return [], text  # malformed frontmatter → treat as no frontmatter
112	
113	
114	def body_of(text: str) -> str:
115	    return split_frontmatter(text)[1]
116	
117	
118	def frontmatter_line_diff(up_text: str, cur_text: str):
119	    """Line-level added/removed on the YAML frontmatter only, after prefix
120	    normalization. ORDER-INSENSITIVE for skills-list entries (set semantics),
121	    which also correctly handles writer.md's preserved duplicate
122	    'creative-writing-craft' line (boundary-contract.md §3.3)."""
123	    up_fm = {ln.rstrip() for ln in split_frontmatter(up_text)[0] if ln.strip()}
124	    cur_fm = {ln.rstrip() for ln in split_frontmatter(cur_text)[0] if ln.strip()}
125	    added = sorted(cur_fm - up_fm)
126	    removed = sorted(up_fm - cur_fm)
127	    return added, removed

130	# --- Upstream dereference (only when --upstream DIR is provided) -----------------
131	def upstream_root(upstream_dir: str) -> Path:
132	    return Path(upstream_dir).resolve() / "cw"
133	
134	
135	def upstream_path(upstream_dir: str, rel: str) -> Path:
136	    return upstream_root(upstream_dir) / rel
137	
138	
139	def upstream_has(upstream_dir: str, rel: str) -> bool:
140	    return upstream_path(upstream_dir, rel).exists()
141	
142	
143	def upstream_blob(upstream_dir: str, rel: str) -> str:
144	    return read_text(upstream_path(upstream_dir, rel))

147	def _checkout_head(upstream_dir: str):
148	    """Read the HEAD commit SHA of the --upstream checkout (CH-5, M3). Returns the
149	    40-hex SHA, or None if git is unavailable or the dir is not a git repo (e.g. a
150	    tarball checkout) — caller then FAILs loud rather than trusting the tree.
151	    `subprocess` is stdlib; only invoked in Mode U."""
152	    try:
153	        out = subprocess.run(
154	            ["git", "-C", str(Path(upstream_dir).resolve()), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
155	            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, timeout=10)
156	        head = out.stdout.strip()
157	        return head or None
158	    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
159	        return None
160	
161	
162	# --- VENDOR.md manifest parsing -------------------------------------------------
163	class Row:
164	    __slots__ = ("path", "cls", "upstream_sha256", "laf_sha256")
165	
166	    def __init__(self, path, cls, up, laf):
167	        self.path = path
168	        self.cls = cls
169	        self.upstream_sha256 = up
170	        self.laf_sha256 = laf
171	
172	    @property
173	    def is_adopted(self):
174	        return self.cls in ("ADOPTED-CLEAN", "ADOPTED-PATCHED")
175	
176	    @property
177	    def is_glob(self):
178	        return self.path.endswith("/**")

181	def _norm_hash(cell: str) -> str:
182	    cell = cell.strip()
183	    if cell in ("", "-", "--", NO_HASH, "<hash>"):
184	        return NO_HASH
185	    return cell
186	
187	
188	def _is_hex64(c: str) -> bool:
189	    """True iff c is a 64-char lowercase/uppercase hex string (a sha256 digest)."""
190	    return len(c) == 64 and all(ch in "0123456789abcdef" for ch in c.lower())
191	
192	
193	def _safe_repo_path(rel: str) -> Path:
194	    """Resolve a manifest path relative to REPO and refuse escapes (CH-4, M2).
195	
196	    A literal `|` inside a path is impossible here (the parser splits on `|`
197	    and rejects rows that don't yield exactly 4 cells — see parse_manifest), so
198	    the only escape vectors are absolute paths and `..` traversal. Both resolve
199	    outside REPO and are rejected as ManifestError. REPO is resolved (absolute)
200	    so a symlinked work-tree cannot smuggle a path back inside.
201	
202	    A manifest entry that resolves to REPO itself (`.` or an empty path) is also
203	    rejected: such a row is never a legitimate file (it would crash read_text on
204	    the directory in Rules A/C), so we fail loud at the parser boundary rather
205	    than letting an IsADirectoryError escape mid-rule."""
206	    if rel.strip() == "" or rel.strip() == ".":
207	        raise ManifestError(f"{rel!r}: manifest path is empty or REPO itself — must name a file")
208	    if Path(rel).is_absolute():
209	        raise ManifestError(f"{rel!r}: manifest path is absolute — must be relative to laf-adaptation/")
210	    resolved = (REPO / rel).resolve()
211	    repo_resolved = REPO.resolve()
212	    # Containment: resolved must be STRICTLY under REPO (a child, not REPO itself).
213	    # The `resolved == repo_resolved` case is rejected above for non-empty/non-dot
214	    # inputs too, because a `..` chain that lands exactly on REPO is not a file.
215	    if resolved == repo_resolved or repo_resolved not in resolved.parents:
216	        raise ManifestError(f"{rel!r}: manifest path escapes laf-adaptation/ tree")
217	    return resolved
218	
219	
220	def parse_manifest(text: str):
221	    """Parse the 4-column manifest table (path | class | upstream_sha256 |
222	    laf_sha256). Returns (rows, errors) where errors is a list[str] of
223	    malformed / duplicate / bad-hash / unsafe-path findings (CH-6, M4 + CH-4, M2).
224	
225	    A security-boundary parser must FAIL LOUD: a silently-dropped row would
226	    un-protect its file. Header/separator rows are still skipped silently. A
227	    literal `|` inside a path/hash shifts columns → the row yields ≠4 cells →
228	    loud failure (paths/hashes must not contain `|`; documented in VENDOR.md)."""
229	    rows, errors = [], []
230	    seen_paths = {}  # path -> first lineno (duplicate detection)
231	    for lineno, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
232	        s = line.strip()
233	        if not s.startswith("|"):
234	            continue
235	        cells = [c.strip() for c in s.strip("|").split("|")]
236	        if len(cells) != 4:
237	            errors.append(f"manifest line {lineno}: expected 4 cells, got {len(cells)}: {s!r}")
238	            continue
239	        path, cls = cells[0], cells[1]
240	        # Header / separator-row detection. Must be PRECISE: a silently-dropped
241	        # data row un-protects its file (CH-6 principle). The only legitimate
242	        # non-data rows are (a) the exact 'path' header and (b) the all-dashes
243	        # separator ('---', non-empty, dashes only). Anything else — including
244	        # an empty path cell, a single space, or ':'-only — is a malformed data
245	        # row and must fail loud. The previous `set(path) <= set("-: ")` test
246	        # admitted the empty string (set() is a subset of every set), silently
247	        # swallowing empty-path rows.
248	        is_header = path.lower() == "path"
249	        is_separator = len(path) >= 1 and set(path) <= {"-"}
250	        if is_header or is_separator:
251	            continue
252	        if cls.upper() not in CLASSES:
253	            errors.append(f"manifest line {lineno}: unknown class {cls!r}")
254	            continue
255	        if path in seen_paths:
256	            errors.append(f"manifest line {lineno}: duplicate path {path!r} (first at line {seen_paths[path]})")
257	            continue
258	        seen_paths[path] = lineno
259	        # Path safety (CH-4): reject absolute / escaping paths loud, not silent.
260	        try:
261	            _safe_repo_path(path)
262	        except ManifestError as e:
263	            errors.append(f"manifest line {lineno}: {e}")
264	            continue
265	        up, laf = _norm_hash(cells[2]), _norm_hash(cells[3])
266	        if cls.upper() in ("ADOPTED-CLEAN", "ADOPTED-PATCHED"):
267	            if not _is_hex64(up) or not _is_hex64(laf):
268	                errors.append(f"manifest line {lineno}: {path!r} adopted row needs 64-hex hashes")
269	                continue
270	        else:  # NATIVE / BUILD-NEW
271	            if up != NO_HASH or laf != NO_HASH:
272	                errors.append(f"manifest line {lineno}: {path!r} {cls.upper()} row must have {NO_HASH} hashes")
273	                continue
274	        rows.append(Row(path, cls.upper(), up, laf))
275	    return rows, errors

278	def parse_upstream_sha(text: str):

282	    parser ignores header lines; this re-reads the header prose for the pin.
283	    The em-dash NO_HASH placeholder and empty/whitespace values are treated as
284	    'unset' (return None) — otherwise a header `upstream_sha: —` would be
285	    treated as a truthy pin and produce a misleading HEAD-mismatch error
286	    instead of the clearer 'no pin' failure."""
287	    for line in text.splitlines():
288	        s = line.strip()
289	        if s.lower().startswith("upstream_sha:") and ":" in s:
290	            val = s.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
291	            if val and val != NO_HASH:
292	                return val
293	    return None

339	        return "NATIVE"
340	    if parts[0] == "skills" and len(parts) >= 2:
341	        sk = parts[1]
342	        if sk in BUILD_NEW_SKILLS:
343	            return "BUILD-NEW"
344	        return "NATIVE"
345	    return "NATIVE"
346	
347	
348	# --- --init: compute hashes + (re)write manifest rows ---------------------------
349	def do_init(upstream_dir: str, upstream_sha=None):
350	    if not upstream_dir:
351	        print("ERROR: --init requires --upstream <dir> (a checkout of the upstream repo "
352	              "at upstream_sha) to record upstream_sha256 and prove the prefix rewrite is "
353	              "the only transformation.", file=sys.stderr)
354	        return 2
355	    if not upstream_root(upstream_dir).is_dir():
356	        print(f"ERROR: --upstream {upstream_dir!r} has no cw/ subtree at "
357	              f"{upstream_root(upstream_dir)}", file=sys.stderr)
358	        return 2
359	    if not VENDOR_MD.exists():
360	        print(f"ERROR: {VENDOR_MD} not found — author the VENDOR.md header + Manifest "
361	              f"table header first (Step 2.12).", file=sys.stderr)
362	        return 2
363	
364	    vendor_text = read_text(VENDOR_MD)
365	    existing_rows, manifest_errors = parse_manifest(vendor_text)
366	    if manifest_errors:
367	        print(f"ERROR: VENDOR.md manifest is malformed — refusing to --init:",
368	              file=sys.stderr)
369	        for e in manifest_errors:
370	            print(f"  - {e}", file=sys.stderr)
371	        return 1
372	    declared = {r.path: r.cls for r in existing_rows}
373	
374	    rows = []          # (path, cls, upstream_sha256, laf_sha256)
375	    warnings = []
376	
377	    # Agents — one row per file
378	    for rel in disk_agents():
379	        cls = classify(rel, declared, upstream_dir)
380	        if cls in ("ADOPTED-CLEAN", "ADOPTED-PATCHED"):
381	            up_raw = upstream_blob(upstream_dir, rel)
382	            up_sha = sha256_text(up_raw)
383	            laf_sha = sha256_text(read_text(_safe_repo_path(rel)))
384	            rows.append((rel, cls, up_sha, laf_sha))
385	        else:
386	            rows.append((rel, cls, NO_HASH, NO_HASH))
387	
388	    # Skills — adopted: per-file rows (SKILL.md + resources/**); native/build-new: one /** row
389	    for skdir in disk_skill_dirs():
390	        sk = skdir.name
391	        skill_rel = f"skills/{sk}"
392	        adopted = bool(upstream_dir) and upstream_root(upstream_dir).joinpath("skills", sk).is_dir()
393	        if adopted:
394	            for rel in disk_skill_files(skdir):
395	                if upstream_has(upstream_dir, rel):
396	                    up_sha = sha256_text(upstream_blob(upstream_dir, rel))
397	                    laf_sha = sha256_text(read_text(_safe_repo_path(rel)))
398	                    rows.append((rel, "ADOPTED-CLEAN", up_sha, laf_sha))
399	                else:
400	                    # a file present in laf's adopted skill but absent upstream → suspicious
401	                    warnings.append(f"{rel}: in an adopted skill dir but absent upstream — "
402	                                    f"labeled ADOPTED-CLEAN, Rule B will flag it")
403	                    laf_sha = sha256_text(read_text(_safe_repo_path(rel)))
404	                    rows.append((rel, "ADOPTED-CLEAN", NO_HASH, laf_sha))
405	        else:
406	            cls = classify(f"{skill_rel}/SKILL.md", declared, upstream_dir)
407	            rows.append((f"{skill_rel}/**", cls, NO_HASH, NO_HASH))
408	
409	    # Order: adopted first, then native, then build-new; stable by path within group
410	    order = {"ADOPTED-CLEAN": 0, "ADOPTED-PATCHED": 0, "NATIVE": 1, "BUILD-NEW": 2}
411	    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (order.get(r[1], 3), r[0]))
412	
413	    _write_manifest_rows(vendor_text, rows)
414	
415	    # F1 (CH-5 re-vendor flow): BEFORE the post-write verify() call, rewrite the
416	    # VENDOR.md `upstream_sha:` header to the checkout's current HEAD. Without
417	    # this, CH-5's HEAD-pin compares the NEW checkout HEAD (the sha being vendored)
418	    # against the stale OLD pinned sha still in the header → a legitimate re-vendor
419	    # spuriously FAILs at exit. Source precedence for the new pin:
420	    #   1. _checkout_head(upstream_dir) — the actual HEAD (normal git-checkout path)
421	    #   2. explicit --upstream-sha flag — tarball/no-git fallback (F3)
422	    #   3. neither → leave the header as-is and let CH-5 fail loud below (do NOT
423	    #      silently trust the tree). The normal `--init --upstream <git checkout>`
424	    #      re-vendor path documented in VENDOR.md lines 32-35 MUST succeed.
425	    new_pin = _checkout_head(upstream_dir) or upstream_sha
426	    if new_pin:
427	        _write_upstream_sha_header(new_pin)
428	        print(f"--init: pinned upstream_sha: header to {new_pin[:12]}…")
429	
430	    adopted_n = sum(1 for r in rows if r[1] in ("ADOPTED-CLEAN", "ADOPTED-PATCHED"))
431	    native_n = sum(1 for r in rows if r[1] == "NATIVE")
432	    buildnew_n = sum(1 for r in rows if r[1] == "BUILD-NEW")
433	    print(f"--init: wrote {len(rows)} manifest rows to {VENDOR_MD.name} "
434	          f"({adopted_n} adopted, {native_n} native, {buildnew_n} build-new).")
435	    for w in warnings:
436	        print(f"  WARNING: {w}")
437	
438	    # Self-check: run verify against the freshly written manifest + upstream.
439	    print("--init: running post-write verification …")
440	    return verify(upstream_dir, upstream_sha)
441	
442	
443	def _write_manifest_rows(vendor_text: str, rows):
444	    lines = vendor_text.splitlines()
445	    header_idx = None
446	    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
447	        s = ln.strip().lower()
448	        if s.startswith("| path") and "class" in s and "sha256" in s:
449	            header_idx = i
450	            break
451	    if header_idx is None:
452	        raise SystemExit("ERROR: VENDOR.md has no '| path | class | upstream_sha256 | "
453	                         "laf_sha256 |' manifest header (author it in Step 2.12).")
454	    sep_idx = header_idx + 1  # the |---|---| separator row
455	    kept = lines[: sep_idx + 1]
456	    body = [f"| {p} | {c} | {u} | {l} |" for (p, c, u, l) in rows]
457	    VENDOR_MD.write_text("\n".join(kept + body) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
458	
459	
460	def _write_upstream_sha_header(sha: str):
461	    """Rewrite the VENDOR.md `upstream_sha:` header line in-place to `sha` (F1).
462	
463	    The re-vendor flow (do_init) computes manifest rows from a freshly-checked-out
464	    upstream; this captures the checkout's HEAD into the header so the post-write
465	    verify()'s CH-5 HEAD-pin sees the NEW sha rather than the stale prior pin.
466	    Idempotent: re-reads the current file, replaces the first `upstream_sha:` line,
467	    preserves every other line byte-for-byte. If no header line exists, this is a
468	    no-op (the VENDOR.md format contract requires one; verify() will report it)."""
469	    lines = VENDOR_MD.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
470	    out, replaced = [], False
471	    for ln in lines:
472	        s = ln.strip().lower()
473	        if s.startswith("upstream_sha:") and ":" in s:
474	            # Preserve original indentation + the field's key spelling.
475	            prefix = ln[: ln.index(":") + 1]
476	            out.append(f"{prefix} {sha}")
477	            replaced = True
478	        else:
479	            out.append(ln)
480	    if replaced:
481	        VENDOR_MD.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
482	
483	
484	# --- verify (default mode) ------------------------------------------------------
485	def verify(upstream_dir=None, upstream_sha=None) -> int:
486	    if not VENDOR_MD.exists():
487	        print(f"ERROR: {VENDOR_MD} not found", file=sys.stderr)
488	        return 1
489	    rows, manifest_errors = parse_manifest(read_text(VENDOR_MD))
490	    if not rows and not manifest_errors:
491	        print("ERROR: VENDOR.md manifest has no rows — run --init --upstream <dir> first.",
492	              file=sys.stderr)
493	        return 1
494	
495	    errors = list(manifest_errors)  # malformed/duplicate/bad-hash rows fail the gate (CH-6)
496	    by_path = {r.path: r for r in rows}
497	
498	    # A. Adopted files match their recorded LAF hash (catches ANY edit)
499	    for r in rows:
500	        if not r.is_adopted:
501	            continue
502	        fp = _safe_repo_path(r.path)  # path already parser-validated; safe by construction here
503	        if not fp.exists():
504	            errors.append(f"{r.path}: adopted file missing from tree")
505	            continue
506	        if sha256_text(read_text(fp)) != r.laf_sha256:
507	            errors.append(f"{r.path}: modified since vendoring (laf_sha256 mismatch)")
508	
509	    # A′. (CH-1, H1) Re-anchor ADOPTED-CLEAN integrity to the PR-rewrite-resistant
510	    # `upstream_sha256` — breaks the self-referential `laf_sha256` loop. The on-disk
511	    # body is the prefix-rewritten upstream, so inverting the rewrite recovers the
512	    # raw upstream blob whose hash `upstream_sha256` pins. A commit that edits an
513	    # adopted body AND rewrites only `laf_sha256` now FAILS here (the body no longer
514	    # inverts to the pinned raw-upstream hash). Runs in BOTH modes (no upstream tree
515	    # needed) — zero CI cost. (Adopted rows are CH-6-validated to carry a 64-hex
516	    # upstream_sha256, so NO_HASH here would itself be a parser error already raised.)
517	    # ADOPTED-PATCHED (writer.md) is intentionally excluded: its `upstream_sha256` is
518	    # the whole-raw-upstream-file hash, not reconstructible from the patched disk
519	    # without the upstream blob; its absolute guarantee is Mode-U Rule C.
520	    for r in rows:
521	        if r.cls != "ADOPTED-CLEAN":
522	            continue
523	        fp = _safe_repo_path(r.path)
524	        if not fp.exists():
525	            continue  # already reported under Rule A
526	        derived = sha256_text(prefix_unrewrite(read_text(fp)))
527	        if derived != r.upstream_sha256:
528	            errors.append(
529	                f"{r.path}: body no longer matches pinned upstream_sha256 — "
530	                f"raw-upstream hash mismatch (CH-1; laf_sha256 rewrite detected)")
531	
532	    # C′. (CH-3, M1) ADOPTED-PATCHED is reserved for agents/writer.md only. Runs in
533	    # BOTH modes (needs no upstream tree) — placed outside the `if upstream_dir:` block.
534	    for r in rows:
535	        if r.cls == "ADOPTED-PATCHED" and r.path != "agents/writer.md":
536	            errors.append(f"{r.path}: ADOPTED-PATCHED is reserved for agents/writer.md only")
537	
538	    # B. ADOPTED-CLEAN == upstream-after-prefix-rewrite (needs upstream)
539	    if upstream_dir:
540	        # CH-5 (M3): before trusting any upstream blob, assert the checkout's HEAD
541	        # equals VENDOR.md's pinned `upstream_sha`. A stale/wrong checkout would
542	        # silently false-green Rules B/C. Pin source precedence: explicit
543	        # --upstream-sha flag > VENDOR.md header `upstream_sha:`. If neither yields
544	        # a pin, FAIL LOUD (do not silently trust the tree). Runs only in Mode U —
545	        # zero cost in Mode V / CI.
546	        #
547	        # Tarball/no-git fallback (F3): if HEAD is unreadable (no git / not a repo)
548	        # BUT an explicit --upstream-sha was supplied, SKIP the HEAD-mismatch check
549	        # — the operator has asserted the pin explicitly, so we do not need to
550	        # re-derive it from git. Rules B/C still run against the supplied tree, so
551	        # the security stance (never silently trust an unverifiable tree) is
552	        # preserved: the pin is an operator assertion, not an inference. Only fail
553	        # loud when there is NO explicit pin AND no readable HEAD.
554	        pinned = upstream_sha or parse_upstream_sha(read_text(VENDOR_MD))
555	        if not pinned:
556	            errors.append("Mode U: no pinned upstream_sha (set upstream_sha: in VENDOR.md "
557	                          "or pass --upstream-sha) — refusing to trust the checkout")
558	        else:
559	            head = _checkout_head(upstream_dir)
560	            if head is None and upstream_sha is None:
561	                errors.append(f"Mode U: could not read HEAD of --upstream {upstream_dir!r} "
562	                              f"(not a git repo / git unavailable) — pass --upstream-sha "
563	                              f"to assert the pin explicitly")
564	            elif head is not None and head != pinned:
565	                errors.append(f"Mode U: --upstream checkout HEAD {head[:12]} != pinned "
566	                              f"upstream_sha {pinned[:12]} (re-checkout at the pinned SHA)")
567	        for r in rows:
568	            if r.cls != "ADOPTED-CLEAN":
569	                continue
570	            if not upstream_has(upstream_dir, r.path):
571	                errors.append(f"{r.path}: ADOPTED-CLEAN but absent from upstream checkout")
572	                continue
573	            expected = sha256_text(prefix_rewrite(upstream_blob(upstream_dir, r.path)))
574	            if r.laf_sha256 != expected:
575	                errors.append(f"{r.path}: ADOPTED-CLEAN but differs from upstream beyond "
576	                              f"prefix rewrite")
577	
578	        # C. ADOPTED-PATCHED diff is frontmatter-only AND additive (needs upstream)
579	        for r in rows:
580	            if r.cls != "ADOPTED-PATCHED":
581	                continue
582	            if not upstream_has(upstream_dir, r.path):
583	                errors.append(f"{r.path}: ADOPTED-PATCHED but absent from upstream checkout")
584	                continue
585	            up = prefix_rewrite(upstream_blob(upstream_dir, r.path))
586	            cur = read_text(_safe_repo_path(r.path))
587	            if body_of(cur) != body_of(up):
588	                errors.append(f"{r.path}: body changed — adopted agent bodies must be "
589	                              f"byte-identical")
590	            added, removed = frontmatter_line_diff(up, cur)
591	            if removed:
592	                errors.append(f"{r.path}: frontmatter lines removed — patch must be "
593	                              f"additive only ({removed})")
594	            bad = [ln for ln in added if not ln.strip().startswith("- laf-adaptation:")]
595	            if bad:
596	                errors.append(f"{r.path}: only additive `- laf-adaptation:<skill>` skill "
597	                              f"lines are permitted (offending: {bad})")
598	    else:
599	        print("NOTE: verify running without --upstream — Rules B and C (upstream-diff "
600	              "checks) skipped; Rule A hash-match covers adopted-file integrity against the "
601	              "recorded manifest, plus Rules D/E/F.")
602	
603	    # D. Invariant G3 — quartet intact, editor never folded
604	    for name in QUARTET:
605	        p = f"agents/{name}.md"
606	        r = by_path.get(p)
607	        if r is None or r.cls != "ADOPTED-CLEAN" or not (REPO / p).exists():
608	            errors.append(f"G3 violation: {p} must exist as ADOPTED-CLEAN (quartet intact)")
609	
610	    # E. No NATIVE/BUILD-NEW name collides with an upstream file
611	    for r in rows:
612	        if r.cls not in ("NATIVE", "BUILD-NEW"):
613	            continue
614	        if upstream_dir:
615	            if r.is_glob:
616	                sk = r.path[len("skills/"):-len("/**")]
617	                if upstream_root(upstream_dir).joinpath("skills", sk).exists():
618	                    errors.append(f"{r.path}: NATIVE/BUILD-NEW skill shadows upstream "
619	                                  f"skills/{sk}")
620	            elif upstream_has(upstream_dir, r.path):
621	                errors.append(f"{r.path}: NATIVE/BUILD-NEW shadows an upstream file name")
622	        else:
623	            # manifest-only best-effort: a native path also listed as adopted = collision
624	            adopted_paths = {x.path for x in rows if x.is_adopted}
625	            if r.path in adopted_paths:
626	                errors.append(f"{r.path}: NATIVE/BUILD-NEW collides with an ADOPTED row")
627	
628	    # F. Every agents/*.md and skills/**/SKILL.md is listed (or glob-covered) in manifest
629	    for rel in disk_agents() + disk_skill_skillmds():
630	        if not manifest_covers(rows, rel):
631	            errors.append(f"{rel}: not in VENDOR.md manifest")
632	
633	    # F′. (CH-2, H2) Extend Rule F to adopted skills' resources/** — every file under
634	    # an adopted skill dir must be manifest-covered. Without this, deleting a manifest
635	    # row or dropping an untracked file into an adopted skill's resources/ is invisible
636	    # to every CI-mode rule. This makes the manifest's resources/** superset ENFORCED,
637	    # not merely descriptive. NATIVE/BUILD-NEW skill dirs are already covered by their
638	    # `/**` glob rows, so this sub-check targets only adopted skill dirs.
639	    adopted_skill_dirs = {
640	        r.path.split("/")[1] for r in rows
641	        if r.path.startswith("skills/") and r.is_adopted
642	    }
643	    for skdir in disk_skill_dirs():
644	        if skdir.name in adopted_skill_dirs:
645	            for rel in disk_skill_files(skdir):
646	                if not manifest_covers(rows, rel):
647	                    errors.append(f"{rel}: adopted-skill file not in VENDOR.md manifest")
648	
649	    if errors:
650	        print(f"BOUNDARY CONTRACT: FAIL — {len(errors)} violation(s):", file=sys.stderr)
651	        for e in errors:
652	            print(f"  - {e}", file=sys.stderr)
653	        return 1
654	    print("BOUNDARY CONTRACT: PASS — all rules (A-F) satisfied.")
655	    return 0
656	
657	
658	# --- --report (always exit 0) ---------------------------------------------------
659	def do_report() -> int:
660	    if not VENDOR_MD.exists():
661	        print("No VENDOR.md present yet.")
662	        return 0
663	    rows, manifest_errors = parse_manifest(read_text(VENDOR_MD))  # --report: exit 0 always
664	    counts = {}
665	    for r in rows:
666	        counts[r.cls] = counts.get(r.cls, 0) + 1
667	    print("laf-adaptation/ provenance summary (from VENDOR.md)")
668	    print("=" * 52)
669	    for cls in ("ADOPTED-CLEAN", "ADOPTED-PATCHED", "NATIVE", "BUILD-NEW"):
670	        print(f"  {cls:<16} {counts.get(cls, 0)}")
671	    print(f"  {'TOTAL rows':<16} {len(rows)}")
672	    print("-" * 52)
673	    for r in rows:
674	        pin = "hash-pinned" if r.is_adopted else "not pinned"
675	        print(f"  [{r.cls:<15}] {r.path}  ({pin})")
676	    # Manifest errors are warnings in --report (exit 0 is the contract); verify mode
677	    # treats them as FAIL, but --report is a human summary and stays non-blocking.
678	    for e in manifest_errors:
679	        print(f"  WARNING (manifest): {e}")
680	    return 0
681	
682	
683	# --- CLI ------------------------------------------------------------------------
684	def main(argv=None):
685	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
686	        description="Boundary-contract checker for laf-adaptation/ (validation tool, not a runtime).")
687	    ap.add_argument("--init", action="store_true",
688	                    help="compute hashes and (re)write VENDOR.md manifest rows; requires --upstream")
689	    ap.add_argument("--report", action="store_true",
690	                    help="print a human-readable provenance summary; always exit 0")
691	    ap.add_argument("--upstream", metavar="DIR", default=None,
692	                    help="path to a checkout of the upstream repo at upstream_sha")
693	    ap.add_argument("--upstream-sha", metavar="SHA", default=None,
694	                    help="explicit upstream_sha pin (Mode U); used if the checkout is not a "
695	                         "git repo or VENDOR.md has no upstream_sha. Asserts HEAD == pin.")
696	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
697	
698	    if args.init and args.report:
699	        print("ERROR: choose one of --init / --report / (default verify).", file=sys.stderr)
700	        return 2
701	    if args.init:
702	        return do_init(args.upstream, args.upstream_sha)
703	    if args.report:
704	        return do_report()
705	    return verify(args.upstream, args.upstream_sha)
706	
707	
708	if __name__ == "__main__":
709	    sys.exit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""test_check_boundary.py — stdlib unittest suite for check_boundary.py.
3	
4	Covers the PR-1 remediation acceptance criteria (spec §5): clean-corpus
5	regression, CH-1 trust-root, CH-2 resources/** coverage, CH-3 writer-only
6	patch, CH-4 path safety, CH-5 Mode-U HEAD pin, CH-6 parser hardening, and
7	CH-7 prefix-rewrite positive path.
8	
9	Every test builds an isolated fixture tree under tempfile.mkdtemp() and
10	points the module globals `check_boundary.REPO` / `check_boundary.VENDOR_MD`
11	at it, so the REAL laf-adaptation/ tree is never mutated (file-scope
12	invariant). Run via:
13	
14	    uv run python scripts/test_check_boundary.py
15	"""
16	
17	import shutil
18	import sys
19	import tempfile
20	import unittest
21	from pathlib import Path
22	
23	# Make the sibling check_boundary.py importable regardless of cwd.
24	_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
25	if str(_HERE) not in sys.path:
26	    sys.path.insert(0, str(_HERE))
27	
28	import check_boundary  # noqa: E402
29	
30	
31	# --- Fixture content helpers ---------------------------------------------------
32	# Adopted-fixture bodies intentionally contain NO "creative-writing-skills:"
33	# literal, so prefix_rewrite() is a no-op and the raw-upstream hash equals
34	# the on-disk hash. (The prefix-rewrite positive path is exercised separately
35	# by test_prefix_rewrite_positive with a synthetic literal-bearing blob.)
36	
37	_QUARTET = ["critic", "editor", "reader-sim", "continuity-checker"]
38	
39	
40	def _agent_body(name):
41	    return f"---\nname: {name}\ndescription: adopted agent fixture\n---\n# {name}\nAdopted body.\n"
42	
43	
44	def _writer_body():
45	    # ADOPTED-PATCHED: additive laf-adaptation skills line in frontmatter.
46	    return ("---\nname: writer\ndescription: writer\n"
47	            "skills:\n  - laf-adaptation:adaptation-rules\n"
48	            "---\n# writer\nAdopted body.\n")
49	
50	
51	def _skill_md(name):
52	    return f"---\nname: {name}\ndescription: skill\n---\n# {name}\nSkill body.\n"
53	
54	
55	# --- Shared base: tmp REPO + VENDOR.md builder --------------------------------
56	class BoundaryTestBase(unittest.TestCase):
57	    """Patches check_boundary.REPO / VENDOR_MD at a tmp dir; restores on tear-down."""
58	
59	    def setUp(self):
60	        self._orig_repo = check_boundary.REPO
61	        self._orig_vendor = check_boundary.VENDOR_MD
62	        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="boundary_test_"))
63	        check_boundary.REPO = self.tmp
64	        check_boundary.VENDOR_MD = self.tmp / "VENDOR.md"
65	
66	    def tearDown(self):
67	        check_boundary.REPO = self._orig_repo
68	        check_boundary.VENDOR_MD = self._orig_vendor
69	        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)
70	
71	    # -- low-level fixture writers --
72	    def write_file(self, rel, content):
73	        p = self.tmp / rel
74	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
75	        p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
76	        return p
77	
78	    def write_manifest(self, rows):
79	        """rows: list of (path, cls, upstream_sha256, laf_sha256) ready to emit."""
80	        header = (
81	            "# VENDOR.md fixture\n\n"
82	            "upstream_repo: https://example/upstream\n"
83	            f"upstream_sha:  {check_boundary.NO_HASH}\n"
84	            "prefix_rewrite: \"creative-writing-skills:\" -> \"laf-adaptation:\"\n\n"
85	            "## Manifest\n\n"
86	            "| path | class | upstream_sha256 | laf_sha256 |\n"

1	# VENDOR.md — Adopted-file manifest
2	
3	upstream_repo: https://github.com/haowjy/creative-writing-skills
4	upstream_sha:  3338495f0fabf778720effdda9386ab56d4ebf6e
5	vendored_on:   2026-07-03
6	license:       Apache-2.0 (upstream) — attribution retained per NOTICE
7	prefix_rewrite: "creative-writing-skills:" -> "laf-adaptation:"   # uniform, deterministic
8	
9	## Hash semantics
10	- `upstream_sha256` is the hash of the **RAW upstream blob** (what `--init` records via
11	  `sha256_text(up_raw)` over the un-rewritten upstream bytes). It is upstream-derived and is the
12	  trust root for adopted-file integrity in verify mode (Rule A′, CH-1): the checker applies the
13	  INVERSE prefix rewrite (`laf-adaptation:` → `creative-writing-skills:`) to the on-disk adopted body
14	  and asserts the result hashes to this pinned value. A committer cannot hide an adopted-body edit by
15	  rewriting only `laf_sha256`; forging `upstream_sha256` is a loud, review-visible change to a field
16	  documented as upstream-derived.
17	- `laf_sha256` is the hash of the on-disk (already-prefix-rewritten) file. Still asserted by Rule A.
18	- NATIVE / BUILD-NEW rows carry `—` (NO_HASH) for both columns; an adopted row missing either hash is
19	  a parse error (CH-6).
20	
21	### What Mode V catches — and what it does NOT (documented honestly, no over-claim)
22	Mode V is a **single-field `laf_sha256`-forgery gate**: it catches a malicious PR that edits an
23	adopted body AND rewrites only its `laf_sha256` row (the body no longer inverts to the pinned
24	`upstream_sha256`). Mode V does **NOT** catch a **two-field forgery** — an attack that edits an
25	adopted body AND rewrites BOTH `laf_sha256` AND `upstream_sha256` to be self-consistent. By
26	construction the PR controls both manifest fields, so any manifest-only re-hash is self-consistent.
27	The two-field forgery is caught only by:
28	1. **Mode U** (Rules B/C against a pinned-SHA upstream checkout) — the mutated body diverges from the
29	   real upstream blob at the pinned SHA, so Rule B fails loud.
30	2. **Branch protection** — any `upstream_sha256` diff is review-visible.
31	3. **Mandatory human review of any `upstream_sha256` diff in a PR** — a field documented as
32	   upstream-derived must not change silently; a reviewer rejects a body+both-hashes change unless it
33	   arrives via the documented `--init` re-vendor flow (see the re-vendor block below).
34	
35	## Format constraint
36	Paths and hashes must not contain a literal `|` (the table delimiter). A `|`-in-cell row shifts
37	columns and is rejected loud by the parser (CH-6) rather than silently dropped.
38	
39	## Invariants (asserted by check_boundary.py)
40	- G3 quartet-intact: agents/{critic,editor,reader-sim,continuity-checker}.md are ADOPTED-CLEAN and present.
41	- editor.md is NEVER folded, NEVER modified.
42	- No NATIVE/BUILD-NEW file name collides with an upstream file name.
43	- ADOPTED-PATCHED is reserved for agents/writer.md only (CH-3).

1	name: Boundary Contract
2	
3	# The ONLY CI this framework ships (ADR-006: prompt + YAML-config, not software —
4	# no test/build matrix). It runs the boundary-contract gate in verify mode (Mode V),
5	# which needs NO --upstream checkout. The rules enforced on the vendored tree +
6	# the VENDOR.md manifest alone are:
7	#   A  — every adopted file matches its recorded laf_sha256 (catches ANY accidental edit)
8	#   A′ — every ADOPTED-CLEAN body re-derives, via the inverse prefix rewrite, to its
9	#        pinned upstream_sha256 (CH-1/H1). This re-anchors adopted-file integrity to
10	#        the upstream-derived hash, so a commit that edits an adopted body AND rewrites
11	#        only its laf_sha256 row FAILS (the body no longer matches the pinned
12	#        upstream_sha256). Forging upstream_sha256 is a loud, review-visible change to a
13	#        field documented as upstream-derived. Mode V is therefore a SINGLE-FIELD
14	#        laf_sha256-forgery gate. It does NOT catch a two-field forgery (rewriting BOTH
15	#        laf_sha256 AND upstream_sha256 to be self-consistent) — that bypasses Mode V
16	#        by construction and is caught only by Mode U (Rules B/C against a pinned-SHA
17	#        upstream checkout) plus branch protection + mandatory human review of any
18	#        upstream_sha256 diff. See VENDOR.md "Hash semantics" for the full statement.
19	#   C′ — ADOPTED-PATCHED is reserved for agents/writer.md (CH-3/M1)
20	#   D  — quartet intact (critic/editor/reader-sim/continuity-checker ADOPTED-CLEAN)
21	#   E  — no NATIVE/BUILD-NEW name collides with an upstream file
22	#   F  — every agents/*.md and skills/**/SKILL.md is manifested
23	#   F′ — every file under an adopted skill's resources/** is manifested (CH-2/H2)
24	# Plus parser hardening (CH-6/M4) and path-safety (CH-4/M2): malformed/duplicate/
25	# bad-hash rows and path-traversal/absolute manifest paths FAIL loud.
26	#
27	# What Mode V does NOT do (documented honestly, not over-claimed): it does not check
28	# out the upstream, so Rules B/C (full upstream diff) and the absolute
29	# upstream-anchored guarantee do not run here. ADOPTED-PATCHED (writer.md) and any
30	# literal-bearing body's ABSOLUTE guarantee requires Mode U (`--upstream`), where
31	# CH-5/M3 additionally asserts the checkout HEAD == VENDOR.md's pinned upstream_sha.
32	# Mode U in CI (Option B) is a deferred follow-up (OQ-4); until then branch
33	# protection + human review backstop the residual absolute-guarantee gap.
34	# Blocking: a failure fails the PR / push.
35	
36	on:
37	  push:
38	    branches: [main]
39	  pull_request:
40	    branches: [main]
41	
42	jobs:
43	  check-boundary:
44	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
45	    steps:
46	      - name: Checkout
47	        uses: actions/checkout@v4
48	
49	      - name: Set up uv
50	        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
51	
52	      - name: Boundary contract (verify)
53	        working-directory: laf-adaptation
54	        run: uv run python scripts/check_boundary.py

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""check_boundary.py — the ONLY script in laf-adaptation/ (ADR-006: this is a
3	validation tool, NOT a runtime). It enforces the boundary contract between the
4	ADOPTED upstream CWS subset and LAF's NATIVE / BUILD-NEW additions.
5	
6	It never transforms the framework — it only reads files, computes sha256 hashes,
7	and compares (boundary-contract.md §3, lines 18-19). The one transformation it
8	*models* (never writes) is the deterministic prefix rewrite
9	    "creative-writing-skills:" -> "laf-adaptation:"
10	
11	Modes (boundary-contract.md §3.1):
12	    check_boundary.py                       # verify (default); exit 1 on any violation
13	    check_boundary.py --init --upstream DIR # first vendor: compute hashes, write manifest rows
14	    check_boundary.py --report              # human-readable provenance summary; always exit 0
15	
16	Path rooting: all relative paths resolve against REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
17	(the laf-adaptation/ dir), so `glob("agents/*.md")` is correct no matter the caller's cwd —
18	the task invokes this from the repo root as `uv run python laf-adaptation/scripts/check_boundary.py`
19	(boundary-contract.md §3.2 uses relative globs; this rooting makes them unambiguous).
20	
21	Pure standard library only (no third-party deps — ADR-006 forbids a runtime).
22	"""
23	
24	import argparse
25	import hashlib
26	import subprocess
27	import sys
28	from pathlib import Path
29	
30	# --- Path rooting (Step 2.2 cwd-rooting contract) -------------------------------
31	REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]          # the laf-adaptation/ dir
32	VENDOR_MD = REPO / "VENDOR.md"
33	
34	# --- The deterministic prefix rewrite -------------------------------------------
35	PREFIX_FROM = "creative-writing-skills:"
36	PREFIX_TO = "laf-adaptation:"
37	
38	# --- Provenance of LAF-authored (non-upstream) files ----------------------------
39	# Adopted files are auto-detected by presence in the upstream checkout. The files
40	# below do NOT exist upstream; this closed set (DESIGN reconciled counts,
41	# constraint #8) lets --init label NATIVE vs BUILD-NEW deterministically. An
42	# existing manifest row's class is ALWAYS preserved over this map (manifest is the
43	# source of truth); the map only classifies newly-discovered non-upstream files.
44	NATIVE_AGENTS = {"analyst.md", "safety-verifier.md"}
45	BUILD_NEW_AGENTS = {"chronicler.md", "tier-coordinator.md"}
46	NATIVE_SKILLS = {"adaptation-tiers", "adaptation-rules", "source-fidelity"}
47	BUILD_NEW_SKILLS = {"adaptation-safety"}
48	
49	QUARTET = ["critic", "editor", "reader-sim", "continuity-checker"]

52	# Manifest row classes (CH-6): a parser-validated closed set.
53	CLASSES = {"ADOPTED-CLEAN", "ADOPTED-PATCHED", "NATIVE", "BUILD-NEW"}

56	class ManifestError(ValueError):
57	    """Raised when a manifest row is malformed, unsafe, or self-inconsistent.
58	
59	    The parser collects these into the errors list (verify/do_init treat them as
60	    boundary-contract FAIL; --report prints them as warnings but still exits 0)."""

63	# --- Low-level helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
64	def sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
65	    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
66	
67	
68	def sha256_text(text: str) -> str:
69	    return sha256_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
70	
71	
72	def read_bytes(p: Path) -> bytes:

74	
75	
76	def read_text(p: Path) -> str:

80	def prefix_rewrite(text: str) -> str:
81	    """The one permitted vendor-time transform, recomputed (never trusted from a
82	    stored diff): replace every literal 'creative-writing-skills:' with
83	    'laf-adaptation:'."""
84	    return text.replace(PREFIX_FROM, PREFIX_TO)
85	
86	
87	def prefix_unrewrite(text: str) -> str:
88	    """Inverse of prefix_rewrite: 'laf-adaptation:' -> 'creative-writing-skills:'.
89	
90	    Used by verify-mode Rule A′ (CH-1) to re-derive the RAW upstream blob from an
91	    already-prefix-rewritten on-disk adopted body, so its hash can be compared
92	    against the pinned (PR-rewrite-resistant) `upstream_sha256`. The on-disk file
93	    IS the prefix-rewritten upstream (disk == prefix_rewrite(raw_upstream)), so
94	    prefix_unrewrite(disk) == raw_upstream for ADOPTED-CLEAN rows. For files
95	    containing no prefix literal this is a no-op (disk == raw)."""
96	    return text.replace(PREFIX_TO, PREFIX_FROM)

98	
99	def split_frontmatter(text: str):
100	    """Return (frontmatter_lines, body_text). Frontmatter is between the first two
101	    '---' delimiter lines; body is everything after the second '---'
102	    (boundary-contract.md §3.3)."""
103	    lines = text.splitlines()
104	    if not lines or lines[0].strip() != "---":
105	        return [], text
106	    for i in range(1, len(lines)):
107	        if lines[i].strip() == "---":
108	            fm = lines[1:i]
109	            body = "\n".join(lines[i + 1:])
110	            return fm, body
111	    return [], text  # malformed frontmatter → treat as no frontmatter
112	
113	
114	def body_of(text: str) -> str:
115	    return split_frontmatter(text)[1]
116	
117	
118	def frontmatter_line_diff(up_text: str, cur_text: str):
119	    """Line-level added/removed on the YAML frontmatter only, after prefix
120	    normalization. ORDER-INSENSITIVE for skills-list entries (set semantics),
121	    which also correctly handles writer.md's preserved duplicate
122	    'creative-writing-craft' line (boundary-contract.md §3.3)."""
123	    up_fm = {ln.rstrip() for ln in split_frontmatter(up_text)[0] if ln.strip()}
124	    cur_fm = {ln.rstrip() for ln in split_frontmatter(cur_text)[0] if ln.strip()}
125	    added = sorted(cur_fm - up_fm)
126	    removed = sorted(up_fm - cur_fm)
127	    return added, removed

130	# --- Upstream dereference (only when --upstream DIR is provided) -----------------
131	def upstream_root(upstream_dir: str) -> Path:
132	    return Path(upstream_dir).resolve() / "cw"
133	
134	
135	def upstream_path(upstream_dir: str, rel: str) -> Path:
136	    return upstream_root(upstream_dir) / rel

138	
139	def upstream_has(upstream_dir: str, rel: str) -> bool:
140	    return upstream_path(upstream_dir, rel).exists()
141	
142	
143	def upstream_blob(upstream_dir: str, rel: str) -> str:
144	    return read_text(upstream_path(upstream_dir, rel))

147	def _checkout_head(upstream_dir: str):
148	    """Read the HEAD commit SHA of the --upstream checkout (CH-5, M3). Returns the
149	    40-hex SHA, or None if git is unavailable or the dir is not a git repo (e.g. a
150	    tarball checkout) — caller then FAILs loud rather than trusting the tree.
151	    `subprocess` is stdlib; only invoked in Mode U."""
152	    try:
153	        out = subprocess.run(
154	            ["git", "-C", str(Path(upstream_dir).resolve()), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
155	            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, timeout=10)
156	        head = out.stdout.strip()
157	        return head or None
158	    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
159	        return None
160

162	# --- VENDOR.md manifest parsing -------------------------------------------------
163	class Row:
164	    __slots__ = ("path", "cls", "upstream_sha256", "laf_sha256")
165	
166	    def __init__(self, path, cls, up, laf):
167	        self.path = path
168	        self.cls = cls
169	        self.upstream_sha256 = up
170	        self.laf_sha256 = laf
171	
172	    @property
173	    def is_adopted(self):
174	        return self.cls in ("ADOPTED-CLEAN", "ADOPTED-PATCHED")
175	
176	    @property

178	        return self.path.endswith("/**")

181	def _norm_hash(cell: str) -> str:
182	    cell = cell.strip()
183	    if cell in ("", "-", "--", NO_HASH, "<hash>"):
184	        return NO_HASH
185	    return cell
186

188	def _is_hex64(c: str) -> bool:
189	    """True iff c is a 64-char lowercase/uppercase hex string (a sha256 digest)."""
190	    return len(c) == 64 and all(ch in "0123456789abcdef" for ch in c.lower())
191	
192	
193	def _safe_repo_path(rel: str) -> Path:
194	    """Resolve a manifest path relative to REPO and refuse escapes (CH-4, M2).
195	
196	    A literal `|` inside a path is impossible here (the parser splits on `|`
197	    and rejects rows that don't yield exactly 4 cells — see parse_manifest), so
198	    the only escape vectors are absolute paths and `..` traversal. Both resolve
199	    outside REPO and are rejected as ManifestError. REPO is resolved (absolute)
200	    so a symlinked work-tree cannot smuggle a path back inside.
201	
202	    A manifest entry that resolves to REPO itself (`.` or an empty path) is also
203	    rejected: such a row is never a legitimate file (it would crash read_text on
204	    the directory in Rules A/C), so we fail loud at the parser boundary rather
205	    than letting an IsADirectoryError escape mid-rule."""
206	    if rel.strip() == "" or rel.strip() == ".":
207	        raise ManifestError(f"{rel!r}: manifest path is empty or REPO itself — must name a file")
208	    if Path(rel).is_absolute():
209	        raise ManifestError(f"{rel!r}: manifest path is absolute — must be relative to laf-adaptation/")
210	    resolved = (REPO / rel).resolve()
211	    repo_resolved = REPO.resolve()
212	    # Containment: resolved must be STRICTLY under REPO (a child, not REPO itself).
213	    # The `resolved == repo_resolved` case is rejected above for non-empty/non-dot
214	    # inputs too, because a `..` chain that lands exactly on REPO is not a file.
215	    if resolved == repo_resolved or repo_resolved not in resolved.parents:
216	        raise ManifestError(f"{rel!r}: manifest path escapes laf-adaptation/ tree")
217	    return resolved
218

220	def parse_manifest(text: str):
221	    """Parse the 4-column manifest table (path | class | upstream_sha256 |
222	    laf_sha256). Returns (rows, errors) where errors is a list[str] of
223	    malformed / duplicate / bad-hash / unsafe-path findings (CH-6, M4 + CH-4, M2).
224	
225	    A security-boundary parser must FAIL LOUD: a silently-dropped row would
226	    un-protect its file. Header/separator rows are still skipped silently. A
227	    literal `|` inside a path/hash shifts columns → the row yields ≠4 cells →
228	    loud failure (paths/hashes must not contain `|`; documented in VENDOR.md)."""
229	    rows, errors = [], []
230	    seen_paths = {}  # path -> first lineno (duplicate detection)
231	    for lineno, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
232	        s = line.strip()
233	        if not s.startswith("|"):
234	            continue
235	        cells = [c.strip() for c in s.strip("|").split("|")]
236	        if len(cells) != 4:
237	            errors.append(f"manifest line {lineno}: expected 4 cells, got {len(cells)}: {s!r}")
238	            continue
239	        path, cls = cells[0], cells[1]

248	        is_header = path.lower() == "path"
249	        is_separator = len(path) >= 1 and set(path) <= {"-"}

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""test_check_boundary.py — stdlib unittest suite for check_boundary.py.
3	
4	Covers the PR-1 remediation acceptance criteria (spec §5): clean-corpus
5	regression, CH-1 trust-root, CH-2 resources/** coverage, CH-3 writer-only
6	patch, CH-4 path safety, CH-5 Mode-U HEAD pin, CH-6 parser hardening, and
7	CH-7 prefix-rewrite positive path.
8	
9	Every test builds an isolated fixture tree under tempfile.mkdtemp() and
10	points the module globals `check_boundary.REPO` / `check_boundary.VENDOR_MD`
11	at it, so the REAL laf-adaptation/ tree is never mutated (file-scope
12	invariant). Run via:
13	
14	    uv run python scripts/test_check_boundary.py
15	"""

17	import shutil
18	import sys
19	import tempfile
20	import unittest
21	from pathlib import Path
22	
23	# Make the sibling check_boundary.py importable regardless of cwd.
24	_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
25	if str(_HERE) not in sys.path:
26	    sys.path.insert(0, str(_HERE))
27	
28	import check_boundary  # noqa: E402
29	
30	
31	# --- Fixture content helpers ---------------------------------------------------
32	# Adopted-fixture bodies intentionally contain NO "creative-writing-skills:"
33	# literal, so prefix_rewrite() is a no-op and the raw-upstream hash equals
34	# the on-disk hash. (The prefix-rewrite positive path is exercised separately
35	# by test_prefix_rewrite_positive with a synthetic literal-bearing blob.)
36	
37	_QUARTET = ["critic", "editor", "reader-sim", "continuity-checker"]
38	
39	
40	def _agent_body(name):
41	    return f"---\nname: {name}\ndescription: adopted agent fixture\n---\n# {name}\nAdopted body.\n"
42	
43	
44	def _writer_body():
45	    # ADOPTED-PATCHED: additive laf-adaptation skills line in frontmatter.
46	    return ("---\nname: writer\ndescription: writer\n"
47	            "skills:\n  - laf-adaptation:adaptation-rules\n"

55	# --- Shared base: tmp REPO + VENDOR.md builder --------------------------------
56	class BoundaryTestBase(unittest.TestCase):
57	    """Patches check_boundary.REPO / VENDOR_MD at a tmp dir; restores on tear-down."""
58	
59	    def setUp(self):
60	        self._orig_repo = check_boundary.REPO
61	        self._orig_vendor = check_boundary.VENDOR_MD
62	        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="boundary_test_"))
63	        check_boundary.REPO = self.tmp
64	        check_boundary.VENDOR_MD = self.tmp / "VENDOR.md"
65	
66	    def tearDown(self):
67	        check_boundary.REPO = self._orig_repo
68	        check_boundary.VENDOR_MD = self._orig_vendor
69	        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)
70	
71	    # -- low-level fixture writers --
72	    def write_file(self, rel, content):
73	        p = self.tmp / rel
74	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
75	        p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
76	        return p
77	
78	    def write_manifest(self, rows):
79	        """rows: list of (path, cls, upstream_sha256, laf_sha256) ready to emit."""
80	        header = (
81	            "# VENDOR.md fixture\n\n"
82	            "upstream_repo: https://example/upstream\n"
83	            f"upstream_sha:  {check_boundary.NO_HASH}\n"
84	            "prefix_rewrite: \"creative-writing-skills:\" -> \"laf-adaptation:\"\n\n"
85	            "## Manifest\n\n"
86	            "| path | class | upstream_sha256 | laf_sha256 |\n"
87	            "|------|-------|-----------------|------------|\n"
88	        )
89	        body = "\n".join(f"| {p} | {c} | {u} | {l} |" for (p, c, u, l) in rows)
90	        check_boundary.VENDOR_MD.write_text(header + body + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
91	
92	    # -- hash helpers (delegate to the module under test) --
93	    def laf_sha(self, rel):
94	        return check_boundary.sha256_text(check_boundary.read_text(self.tmp / rel))
95	
96	    def upstream_sha_clean(self, rel):
97	        """Raw-upstream hash for a no-literal ADOPTED-CLEAN body.
98	
99	        Matches `--init` line 249 semantics (`sha256_text(up_raw)`): the disk IS the
100	        prefix-rewritten upstream, so the raw upstream = prefix_unrewrite(disk). For
101	        fixture bodies with no `creative-writing-skills:` literal the inverse is a
102	        no-op, so upstream_sha == laf_sha == sha256(disk) — consistent with the real
103	        corpus's no-literal rows."""
104	        return check_boundary.sha256_text(
105	            check_boundary.prefix_unrewrite(check_boundary.read_text(self.tmp / rel)))
106	
107	    def upstream_sha_patched(self, rel):
108	        """Raw-upstream hash for ADOPTED-PATCHED == sha256(prefix_rewrite(body_of(disk)))."""
109	        return check_boundary.sha256_text(
110	            check_boundary.prefix_rewrite(check_boundary.body_of(check_boundary.read_text(self.tmp / rel))))

112	    # -- canonical clean-fixture builder --
113	    def build_clean_fixture(self):

116	        NH = check_boundary.NO_HASH

119	        for name in _QUARTET:

127	        # A NATIVE agent.
128	        nrel = "agents/analyst.md"
129	        self.write_file(nrel, _agent_body("analyst"))
130	        rows.append((nrel, "NATIVE", NH, NH))
131	        # An adopted skill with a SKILL.md + a resources/** file.
132	        sm = "skills/sample/SKILL.md"
133	        self.write_file(sm, _skill_md("sample"))
134	        rows.append((sm, "ADOPTED-CLEAN", self.upstream_sha_clean(sm), self.laf_sha(sm)))
135	        sr = "skills/sample/resources/note.md"
136	        self.write_file(sr, "# note\nresource body\n")
137	        rows.append((sr, "ADOPTED-CLEAN", self.upstream_sha_clean(sr), self.laf_sha(sr)))
138	        # A native skill (glob row).
139	        self.write_file("skills/native1/SKILL.md", _skill_md("native1"))

42	# Remediate check_boundary.py trust-root + resources/** coverage gaps (PR #1 review)
43	
44	## Task Overview
45	
46	This task implements the Phase-A remediation spec for the `laf-adaptation` boundary-contract enforcement layer. The PR-1 review found the framework works correctly for accidental drift, but the *enforcement* has a trust-root gap: in the mode CI actually runs (`check_boundary.py` with no `--upstream`), the trust root is the PR-controlled `VENDOR.md` manifest, not the pinned upstream — so a commit that edits an adopted body AND updates its manifest `laf_sha256` passes CI green. The two HIGH findings (H1 trust-root, H2 `resources/**` coverage) plus 5 MEDIUM hardening findings (M1–M5) are fixed here.
47	
48	**What this task does NOT dispute** (per REVIEW.md): the vendored corpus is byte-faithful, Rules A–F are correct for the accidental-drift case, and the framework's functional behavior is sound. Every change here *strengthens* enforcement robustness against a hostile/malformed manifest; none weaken adopted-file integrity.
49	
50	**This is Phase B — authoring only.** The task file is produced here; execution happens later via `/task <path>`, gated by a `/sc:reflect` analyze pass.

44	## Task Overview

46	This task implements the Phase-A remediation spec for the `laf-adaptation` boundary-contract enforcement layer. 278	def parse_upstream_sha(text: str):
279	    """Read the `upstream_sha:` field from the VENDOR.md header (CH-5, M3).
280	
281	    Returns the SHA string or None if unset/unparseable. The manifest table
282	    parser ignores header lines; this re-reads the header prose for the pin.
283	    The em-dash NO_HASH placeholder and empty/whitespace values are treated as
284	    'unset' (return None) — otherwise a header `upstream_sha: —` would be
285	    treated as a truthy pin and produce a misleading HEAD-mismatch error
286	    instead of the clearer 'no pin' failure."""
287	    for line in text.splitlines():
288	        s = line.strip()
289	        if s.lower().startswith("upstream_sha:") and ":" in s:
290	            val = s.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
291	            if val and val != NO_HASH:
292	                return val
293	    return None

460	def _write_upstream_sha_header(sha: str):
461	    """Rewrite the VENDOR.md `upstream_sha:` header line in-place to `sha` (F1).
462	
463	    The re-vendor flow (do_init) computes manifest rows from a freshly-checked-out
464	    upstream; this captures the checkout's HEAD into the header so the post-write
465	    verify()'s CH-5 HEAD-pin sees the NEW sha rather than the stale prior pin.
466	    Idempotent: re-reads the current file, replaces the first `upstream_sha:` line,
467	    preserves every other line byte-for-byte. If no header line exists, this is a
468	    no-op (the VENDOR.md format contract requires one; verify() will report it)."""
469	    lines = VENDOR_MD.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
470	    out, replaced = [], False
471	    for ln in lines:
472	        s = ln.strip().lower()
473	        if s.startswith("upstream_sha:") and ":" in s:
474	            # Preserve original indentation + the field's key spelling.
475	            prefix = ln[: ln.index(":") + 1]
476	            out.append(f"{prefix} {sha}")
477	            replaced = True
478	        else:
479	            out.append(ln)
480	    if replaced:
481	        VENDOR_MD.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

484	# --- verify (default mode) ------------------------------------------------------
485	def verify(upstream_dir=None, upstream_sha=None) -> int:
486	    if not VENDOR_MD.exists():
487	        print(f"ERROR: {VENDOR_MD} not found", file=sys.stderr)
488	        return 1
489	    rows, manifest_errors = parse_manifest(read_text(VENDOR_MD))
490	    if not rows and not manifest_errors:
491	        print("ERROR: VENDOR.md manifest has no rows — run --init --upstream <dir> first.",
492	              file=sys.stderr)
493	        return 1
494	
495	    errors = list(manifest_errors)  # malformed/duplicate/bad-hash rows fail the gate (CH-6)
496	    by_path = {r.path: r for r in rows}
497	
498	    # A. Adopted files match their recorded LAF hash (catches ANY edit)
499	    for r in rows:
500	        if not r.is_adopted:
501	            continue
502	        fp = _safe_repo_path(r.path)  # path already parser-validated; safe by construction here
503	        if not fp.exists():
504	            errors.append(f"{r.path}: adopted file missing from tree")
505	            continue
506	        if sha256_text(read_text(fp)) != r.laf_sha256:
507	            errors.append(f"{r.path}: modified since vendoring (laf_sha256 mismatch)")
508	
509	    # A′. (CH-1, H1) Re-anchor ADOPTED-CLEAN integrity to the PR-rewrite-resistant
510	    # `upstream_sha256` — breaks the self-referential `laf_sha256` loop. The on-disk
511	    # body is the prefix-rewritten upstream, so inverting the rewrite recovers the
512	    # raw upstream blob whose hash `upstream_sha256` pins. A commit that edits an
513	    # adopted body AND rewrites only `laf_sha256` now FAILS here (the body no longer
514	    # inverts to the pinned raw-upstream hash). Runs in BOTH modes (no upstream tree
515	    # needed) — zero CI cost. (Adopted rows are CH-6-validated to carry a 64-hex
516	    # upstream_sha256, so NO_HASH here would itself be a parser error already raised.)
517	    # ADOPTED-PATCHED (writer.md) is intentionally excluded: its `upstream_sha256` is
518	    # the whole-raw-upstream-file hash, not reconstructible from the patched disk
519	    # without the upstream blob; its absolute guarantee is Mode-U Rule C.
520	    for r in rows:
521	        if r.cls != "ADOPTED-CLEAN":
522	            continue
523	        fp = _safe_repo_path(r.path)
524	        if not fp.exists():
525	            continue  # already reported under Rule A
526	        derived = sha256_text(prefix_unrewrite(read_text(fp)))
527	        if derived != r.upstream_sha256:
528	            errors.append(
529	                f"{r.path}: body no longer matches pinned upstream_sha256 — "
530	                f"raw-upstream hash mismatch (CH-1; laf_sha256 rewrite detected)")
531	
532	    # C′. (CH-3, M1) ADOPTED-PATCHED is reserved for agents/writer.md only. Runs in
533	    # BOTH modes (needs no upstream tree) — placed outside the `if upstream_dir:` block.
534	    for r in rows:
535	        if r.cls == "ADOPTED-PATCHED" and r.path != "agents/writer.md":
536	            errors.append(f"{r.path}: ADOPTED-PATCHED is reserved for agents/writer.md only")
537	
538	    # B. ADOPTED-CLEAN == upstream-after-prefix-rewrite (needs upstream)
539	    if upstream_dir:
540	        # CH-5 (M3): before trusting any upstream blob, assert the checkout's HEAD
541	        # equals VENDOR.md's pinned `upstream_sha`. A stale/wrong checkout would
542	        # silently false-green Rules B/C. Pin source precedence: explicit
543	        # --upstream-sha flag > VENDOR.md header `upstream_sha:`. If neither yields
544	        # a pin, FAIL LOUD (do not silently trust the tree). Runs only in Mode U —
545	        # zero cost in Mode V / CI.
546	        #
547	        # Tarball/no-git fallback (F3): if HEAD is unreadable (no git / not a repo)
548	        # BUT an explicit --upstream-sha was supplied, SKIP the HEAD-mismatch check
549	        # — the operator has asserted the pin explicitly, so we do not need to
550	        # re-derive it from git. Rules B/C still run against the supplied tree, so
551	        # the security stance (never silently trust an unverifiable tree) is
552	        # preserved: the pin is an operator assertion, not an inference. Only fail
553	        # loud when there is NO explicit pin AND no readable HEAD.
554	        pinned = upstream_sha or parse_upstream_sha(read_text(VENDOR_MD))
555	        if not pinned:
556	            errors.append("Mode U: no pinned upstream_sha (set upstream_sha: in VENDOR.md "
557	                          "or pass --upstream-sha) — refusing to trust the checkout")
558	        else:
559	            head = _checkout_head(upstream_dir)

1	name: Boundary Contract
2	
3	# The ONLY CI this framework ships (ADR-006: prompt + YAML-config, not software —
4	# no test/build matrix). It runs the boundary-contract gate in verify mode (Mode V),
5	# which needs NO --upstream checkout. The rules enforced on the vendored tree +
6	# the VENDOR.md manifest alone are:
7	#   A  — every adopted file matches its recorded laf_sha256 (catches ANY accidental edit)
8	#   A′ — every ADOPTED-CLEAN body re-derives, via the inverse prefix rewrite, to its
9	#        pinned upstream_sha256 (CH-1/H1). This re-anchors adopted-file integrity to
10	#        the upstream-derived hash, so a commit that edits an adopted body AND rewrites
11	#        only its laf_sha256 row FAILS (the body no longer matches the pinned
12	#        upstream_sha256). Forging upstream_sha256 is a loud, review-visible change to a
13	#        field documented as upstream-derived. Mode V is therefore a SINGLE-FIELD
14	#        laf_sha256-forgery gate. It does NOT catch a two-field forgery (rewriting BOTH
15	#        laf_sha256 AND upstream_sha256 to be self-consistent) — that bypasses Mode V
16	#        by construction and is caught only by Mode U (Rules B/C against a pinned-SHA
17	#        upstream checkout) plus branch protection + mandatory human review of any
18	#        upstream_sha256 diff. See VENDOR.md "Hash semantics" for the full statement.
19	#   C′ — ADOPTED-PATCHED is reserved for agents/writer.md (CH-3/M1)
20	#   D  — quartet intact (critic/editor/reader-sim/continuity-checker ADOPTED-CLEAN)
21	#   E  — no NATIVE/BUILD-NEW name collides with an upstream file
22	#   F  — every agents/*.md and skills/**/SKILL.md is manifested
23	#   F′ — every file under an adopted skill's resources/** is manifested (CH-2/H2)
24	# Plus parser hardening (CH-6/M4) and path-safety (CH-4/M2): malformed/duplicate/
25	# bad-hash rows and path-traversal/absolute manifest paths FAIL loud.
26	#
27	# What Mode V does NOT do (documented honestly, not over-claimed): it does not check
28	# out the upstream, so Rules B/C (full upstream diff) and the absolute
29	# upstream-anchored guarantee do not run here. ADOPTED-PATCHED (writer.md) and any
30	# literal-bearing body's ABSOLUTE guarantee requires Mode U (`--upstream`), where
31	# CH-5/M3 additionally asserts the checkout HEAD == VENDOR.md's pinned upstream_sha.
32	# Mode U in CI (Option B) is a deferred follow-up (OQ-4); until then branch
33	# protection + human review backstop the residual absolute-guarantee gap.
34	# Blocking: a failure fails the PR / push.
35	
36	on:
37	  push:
38	    branches: [main]
39	  pull_request:
40	    branches: [main]
41	
42	jobs:
43	  check-boundary:
44	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
45	    steps:
46	      - name: Checkout
47	        uses: actions/checkout@v4
48	
49	      - name: Set up uv
50	        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
51	
52	      - name: Boundary contract (verify)
53	        working-directory: laf-adaptation
54	        run: uv run python scripts/check_boundary.py
55

1	# VENDOR.md — Adopted-file manifest
2	
3	upstream_repo: https://github.com/haowjy/creative-writing-skills

9	## Hash semantics
10	- `upstream_sha256` is the hash of the **RAW upstream blob** (what `--init` records via
11	  `sha256_text(up_raw)` over the un-rewritten upstream bytes). It is upstream-derived and is the
12	  trust root for adopted-file integrity in verify mode (Rule A′, CH-1): the checker applies the
13	  INVERSE prefix rewrite (`laf-adaptation:` → `creative-writing-skills:`) to the on-disk adopted body
14	  and asserts the result hashes to this pinned value. A committer cannot hide an adopted-body edit by
15	  rewriting only `laf_sha256`; forging `upstream_sha256` is a loud, review-visible change to a field
16	  documented as upstream-derived.
17	- `laf_sha256` is the hash of the on-disk (already-prefix-rewritten) file. Still asserted by Rule A.
18	- NATIVE / BUILD-NEW rows carry `—` (NO_HASH) for both columns; an adopted row missing either hash is
19	  a parse error (CH-6).
20	
21	### What Mode V catches — and what it does NOT (documented honestly, no over-claim)
22	Mode V is a **single-field `laf_sha256`-forgery gate**: it catches a malicious PR that edits an
23	adopted body AND rewrites only its `laf_sha256` row (the body no longer inverts to the pinned
24	`upstream_sha256`). Mode V does **NOT** catch a **two-field forgery** — an attack that edits an
25	adopted body AND rewrites BOTH `laf_sha256` AND `upstream_sha256` to be self-consistent. By
26	construction the PR controls both manifest fields, so any manifest-only re-hash is self-consistent.
27	The two-field forgery is caught only by:
28	1. **Mode U** (Rules B/C against a pinned-SHA upstream checkout) — the mutated body diverges from the
29	   real upstream blob at the pinned SHA, so Rule B fails loud.
30	2. **Branch protection** — any `upstream_sha256` diff is review-visible.
31	3. **Mandatory human review of any `upstream_sha256` diff in a PR** — a field documented as
32	   upstream-derived must not change silently; a reviewer rejects a body+both-hashes change unless it
33	   arrives via the documented `--init` re-vendor flow (see the re-vendor block below).
34	
35	## Format constraint
36	Paths and hashes must not contain a literal `|` (the table delimiter). A `|`-in-cell row shifts
37	columns and is rejected loud by the parser (CH-6) rather than silently dropped.
38	
39	## Invariants (asserted by check_boundary.py)
40	- G3 quartet-intact: agents/{critic,editor,reader-sim,continuity-checker}.md are ADOPTED-CLEAN and present.
41	- editor.md is NEVER folded, NEVER modified.
42	- No NATIVE/BUILD-NEW file name collides with an upstream file name.
43	- ADOPTED-PATCHED is reserved for agents/writer.md only (CH-3).
44	- Every file under an adopted skill's resources/** is manifested (CH-2).
